findings.F1: Saturday's volatility-scaled return predicts the volatility-scaled return over Monday and Tuesday in the same direction (slope 0.211, t 6.27, 2103 Mondays), and this holds in both halves of the period (2018–2021 t 4.77, 2022–2025 t 3.97). On the other start days, the return from two days back predicts nothing comparable (t between −1.18 and 2.11).
findings.F2: The book's condition that the 7-day return agree with Saturday is not what carries the effect, and calm markets are where it is largest.
findings.F3: The 7-day return at Friday 00:00 UTC predicts the volatility-scaled return over Friday and Saturday in the same direction.
findings.F4: Saturday's own return is positive on average, in both halves and for every coin.
findings.F5: Sunday's volatility-scaled return is partly reversed on Monday, but only in turbulent markets and mostly in the earlier years, so this is the weakest finding.
findings.F6: The book's gain comes from its strongest forecasts and is uneven across years.

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return over Saturday is followed over Monday and Tuesday by a move in the same direction that grows with the size of Saturday's move scaled by the coin's 30-day volatility of hourly returns, while that volatility is low against its own past year, whichever way the coin's 7-day return points.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow Saturday's move into Monday and Tuesday in calm markets without waiting for the week to agree, which roughly doubles the cases available to the tested book.
ideas.name: calm Saturday continuation unfiltered

ideas.idea: A coin's 7-day return, read at the start of Friday, is followed over Friday and Saturday by a move in the same direction that grows with the size of the 7-day return scaled by its 30-day volatility of hourly returns, the more so the lower that volatility is against its own past year.
ideas.consequence: A trader would ride the week's direction through Friday and Saturday, most of all in calm markets, ahead of the Saturday-continuation trade.
ideas.name: weekly momentum into weekend

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return over Sunday is followed on Monday by a move in the opposite direction that grows with the size of Sunday's move scaled by its 30-day volatility of hourly returns, while that volatility is high against its own past year.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean against Sunday's move during Monday in turbulent markets, and refuse to follow Sunday's move into the week.
ideas.name: turbulent Sunday reverses Monday
